evidence.note: Anthropic prospectus, available before the evaluation date. It shows GAAP net losses that are mostly fair-value charges, alongside positive adjusted results. That covers one company and one basis, and says nothing about the moat as a cause.

The study finds frontier gaps come mostly from compute, but some developers have efficiency edges. Its 2022–2025 sample neither proves nor rules out durable moats in 2026, and it does not address profitability.

Spending concentrated in the leaders, despite cheaper alternatives, cuts against simple commoditization. But market share is not proof of a durable technical moat, and the report says nothing on profitability.

reviews.rationale: The packet has losses for one company on one basis, mixed signals on technical differentiation, and no evidence linking a missing moat to profitability across LLM companies. The evidence available by the cutoff neither establishes nor refutes the causal claim.

reviews.rationale: On the contract's fair plain reading, independent analysis shows that circular investor-supplier ties made reported growth hard to separate from financing-supported demand. The packet has no evidence that disclosures cleanly separate these flows.
